decisions.statement: A client registers this and no hook of its own.
The event judged is read from the payload rather than from the link called.
The hooks are the pages the index names as hooks.
A hook naming the tools it is over runs only where the payload names one of them.
A hook naming no tool runs at every call of its event.
The hooks run in the order their slugs sort in.
The first hook to refuse answers the whole call and the rest do not run.
A hook exiting neither let-through nor refused refuses the call it judged.
A hook handing back changed input hands the next hook the input as changed.
A run this cannot make sense of refuses the call rather than letting it through.
A payload naming no event refuses the call.
A hook whose code is not there refuses the call.
A run in the checkout the links serve puts the links back, so a moved dispatch mends itself.
The checkout is found from this file's real path rather than from the link's.
What each hook's run cost is appended beside that hook's own page.
The high-water mark is forgotten once for the call rather than once per hook.
One hook's reading is the reading the next hook's cost is taken from.
The processor time counted is the child's, which is the hook's whole run.
The memory counted is this process's, which the hooks before left as they did.
Every hook run for one call has one run id.
A hook that refused is recorded as a run with one refusal.
A cost that could not be recorded leaves the call as the call was.
No rule any hook judges by is known here.
What event a hook runs at, and what tools it is over, are read from that hook's page.

definition: the one hook a client calls, running every hook the index names for that event
